summary.intent: Act as PM/orchestrator for CipherBox v2, driving multiple in-flight PRs (#716, #707, #726) through CodeRabbit/Greptile review cycles, planning and delegating a crypto-hardening batch PR, launching new build slices (#639) in parallel, and establishing a new fail-closed encode/decode symmetry rule after a recurring debug_assert bug pattern.
summary.outcome: Merged #716; reconciled and fixed a subtle boolean/void PinStore.unpin semantic conflict on #707, then dispatched a fix for CR's unbounded-lock-batch finding; planned and shipped core-hardening batch PR #726 (4 commits, additive-only KAT changes) and dispatched a fix for Greptile's debug_assert release-build footgun; launched #639 (web engine worker) in a new worktree; corrected an earlier wrong premise that #712 blocked #633; recorded the #712 recipient-binding decision; saved a new memory and started an AGENTS.md rule for encode/decode fail-closed symmetry.

repo: X25519Public::from_bytes (crates/core/src/suite/x25519.rs) was totally permissive (no point validation) — fixed in #726 to reject low-order/non-contributory points, converting it to return Option

PinStore.unpin return type is contract-significant: #707's account-delete cascade needs boolean (counts releases via return value at account.service.ts:195) while #723's retire path uses void (counts via in-lock survivor recount) — merges must resolve to whichever caller actually consumes the return, not just pick one side

retire's in-txn per-CID advisory lock (registry.service.ts) guards a different race than the post-commit durability recount: it blocks a concurrent INSERT of a phantom pin row during the delete→survivor window (row lock can't stop an unborn INSERT, per #677); the post-commit recount guards after-commit re-pin (#714) — the two are not redundant

account-delete's unbounded per-CID lock batch is the #677 N+1-lock pattern recurring: quota is bounded by bytes not pin count, so large accounts can have tens of thousands of CIDs, each needing a sequential round-trip lock inside one transaction holding the user-row pessimistic_write lock

Recurring bug class: encode-side dup/uniqueness guards implemented as debug_assert! compile out in release builds, letting a release build emit bytes its own decoder always rejects (grant/body encode paths, and now #726's grant-set/write-body dup-tag guards) — decode-side fail-closed checks are not enough; encode side needs the same enforcement

mailbox sig_preimage in payload/mailbox.rs hashes raw sender_pk bytes, so secp256k1's dual SEC1 encodings (33-byte compressed vs 65-byte uncompressed) of the same key produce two byte-distinct but both-valid messages — fixed via a width guard at EcdsaVerifier::from_sec1 choke point
kdf/mod.rs already documented a low-order/degenerate-key gap ('use the contributory check on the x25519 seam') years before the check was actually implemented in #726

HPKE's dhkem_encap already folds pk_r into kem_context so ciphertext relay to a wrong recipient is impossible — the actual mailbox gap (#712) is signature-attribution (a plaintext holder can re-seal to a third party under a valid original signature), not confidentiality

#712's fix does NOT require a wire-format change — the signed preimage is never transmitted (recomputed both sides), so adding the recipient to it needs no new field; only the signature bytes (and thus ct) change, forcing a KAT vectors regen but not a schema/decoder change

Local Claude Code HTTP hooks (~/.claude/settings.json, matcher '' on every tool) POST to http://127.0.0.1:19847/hook/<token>/<event> for the desktop app's activity feed; background worktree subagents can't reach/authenticate to that listener, producing harmless PostToolUse error logs with no effect on agent work

code.finding: Comment explains the in-txn advisory lock is needed because a row lock can't see an unborn INSERT, making delete→survivor check authoritative — this is the #677 lesson made concrete
deleteAccount cascade feeds PinStore.unpin's boolean return directly into released/unpinned count, which is why unpin must stay boolean post-#707/#716/#723 merge rather than void
Doc comment explicitly stated no point validation was performed on X25519Public::from_bytes prior to #726's fix

sig_preimage signs [domain, v, senderIdentityPk, payload] with no recipient binding — root cause of #712's attribution gap; also root cause of #709's uncompressed-key double-signing issue since it hashes raw sender_pk bytes

workflow: When two open PRs touch the same file (#707 and #716 both edit content.service.ts), defer reconciling the earlier one until the later one merges — reconciling twice (once now, once after) wastes a throwaway merge commit

A textual git merge can auto-resolve conflict markers cleanly while still hiding a semantic conflict (return type contract mismatch) that only surfaces at typecheck/test time — always run typecheck + full unit suite after resolving merge conflicts, don't trust a clean merge alone

Before batching multiple fix issues into one PR, have an agent produce a per-issue KAT/blast-radius analysis (which changes wire bytes vs. purely additive) — this is the real cost driver for review effort, not superficial 'same crate' groupings

Verify a planning subagent's premises independently before acting on them — the core-batch planning agent asserted #712 blocked #633 and characterized it as a wire-format change; both were checked against source and found materially wrong
CodeRabbit's ~1/hr org-wide quota can be anchored/predicted from the timestamp of its last review activity across recent PRs, letting the user time when to ready a PR for CR rather than guessing

Use a background poll (with a time ceiling) to watch for an async bot review landing rather than manually re-checking; kill the poll immediately once superseded by an actual event (e.g., PR merge) to avoid stale background work

When delegating a fix agent whose own root-cause hypothesis might be wrong, explicitly instruct it to verify the hypothesis against the codebase before implementing, and require proof (e.g. adversarial interleave tests) rather than accepting a plausible-sounding redesign

friction: Stale background-task tracker rows for already-shipped work (#632/#630/#636) could not be cleared via TaskStop or /tasks — turned out to be held open by a separate untracked spawned agent the user had to find and kill manually; neither /tasks nor available tools could diagnose or resolve this
A core-batch planning subagent made two materially wrong claims (that #712 blocks #633, and that #712 requires a wire-format change) that had to be caught and corrected by direct source verification
